model_label: Distributable Operating Earnings (FCFE) DCF at cost of equity, component-built; hybrid of the REIT/distributable-profit row and the operating-company engine

inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2026 proportionally consolidated segment revenue (Property Investment 409.4 + Development Investment 93.7 + Funds Management 449.0), FY26 AR note 1(c). NOT the statutory 'funds management revenue' line (556.7) in the Metrics CSV: the statutory line excludes the look-through co-investment income that is ~45% of Operating Earnings.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 472,997,199 stapled securities on issue + 8,542,149 performance rights + 548,051 service rights = 482.09m (FY26 AR note, diluted EPS denominator). Held FLAT: the rights are the only equity compensation and are already in this count; buybacks (A$43.2m FY26) fund the flat count.
inputs.net_debt_note: Deliberately ZERO in the model. The flow being discounted is Operating Earnings, which is already AFTER net interest expense (FY26 A$117.3m = A$26.9m on balance-sheet borrowings + A$90.4m co-investment share of the funds' interest). Deducting the A$505.9m balance-sheet net debt (712.2 borrowings - 206.3 cash) on top would charge the debt twice (dcf-methods SKILL.md: never FCF/WACC on a post-interest flow, never subtract net debt afterwards). total_debt and cash below are recorded for audit only.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026 free cash flow to equity: Operating Earnings 488.1 less retained reinvestment 212.2 (= 488.1 - 232.7 distributions paid - 43.2 buybacks). This is the cash securityholders actually received; the retained half was deployed into co-investments and development, which is what funds the growth path. NOT the statutory FCF of 86.1: FY26 OCF is distorted by the AASB 10 investment-entity election that moved investment purchases/proceeds into operating activities (FY25 comparable OCF 450.8).
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Operating Earnings attributable to stapled securityholders, FY2026 (management's distribution-basis measure; statutory NPAT 427.9 differs by fair-value movements, derivatives and amortisation of management rights). Used as the 'reported' distributable flow in place of statutory FCF (86.1, AASB 10 artefact) or statutory NPAT (dominated by revaluations: FY24 -222.1 on 358.7 of OE).
inputs.sbc_source: Expensed inside Operating Earnings (employee benefits) and NOT added back, so no second deduction is made in the flows; the FY26 filing publishes no separate cash-flow SBC add-back. The equity plan's 9.09m performance/service rights (1.9% of the count) are carried in the diluted share count. House and street bases therefore coincide.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY26 interest received A$5.2m is left inside the flows (it nets within the A$117.3m net interest line) because net debt is not deducted and no cash is added to EV: the excluded-income/matching-asset rule is satisfied in the other direction.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-22T06:10:03Z (ASX regular close 16:00 AEST; Yahoo v8 chart meta; 52w range 17.60-25.95)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Discount rate is the AUD COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flow is post-interest and no net debt is deducted: AUD 10-year government yield ~4.4% (Sept 2026, assumed) + 5.5% equity risk premium x beta 1.0 = 9.9%, rounded to 10.0%. CHC's observed beta is above 1 (property-cycle and rate gearing), but that cyclicality is charged in the bear scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate (owner-fcf.md 7f). One rate across all scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost: lease payments (A$10.6m principal FY26) sit inside Operating Earnings' costs; lease liabilities (A$5.7m) are immaterial and excluded from debt (which is zero in the model anyway).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are attributable-only by construction: Operating Earnings is stated 'attributable to stapled securityholders' and the proportionally consolidated segment build takes only the Group's co-investment share of each fund. No NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.tax_note: Cash tax on operating earnings before tax: FY26 81.9/570.0 = 14.4% (cash tax paid 80.8), FY25 96.4/481.4 = 20.0%. Blended because Charter Hall Property Trust is untaxed (flow-through) while Charter Hall Limited (funds management, development) pays 30%. Modelled at 15.0% flat; a rising funds-management share of earnings would push it up, a rising co-investment share would pull it down.
inputs.engine_mapping: ebitda_margin_path = (Operating earnings before tax + D&A) / proportional revenue, i.e. EBITDA AFTER the A$117.3m look-through net interest (FY26: (570.0+8.9)/952.1 = 60.8%; FY25: (481.4+8.1)/834.2 = 58.7%). da_pct_path = 8.9/952.1 = 0.9%. capex_pct_path = net reinvestment of retained earnings into co-investments/development (management: 'approximately half of the Group's earnings are retained and reinvested to support future growth'); it fades as growth fades so that terminal retention (~25% of post-tax OE) x an incremental return on equity of ~12% supports the 3% terminal growth. cash_tax_rate_path applies to EBIT = operating earnings before tax. FCF out of the engine is therefore free cash flow to equity after growth reinvestment.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Charter Hall straddles two routing rows (externally-managed property trust co-investment book + operating funds-management business). Rather than a sum-of-parts with a separate NTA leg, the group's own single distributable measure, Operating Earnings, is projected and capitalised at the cost of equity with net debt held at zero (REIT-row rule), on the component engine so the dashboard reproduces it. The engine's 'EBITDA' is post-net-interest by construction (see engine_mapping). Sum-of-parts cross-check (memo): NTA A$5.95/security for the co-investment/development book (FY26, after balance-sheet debt) plus the funds-management segment (EBITDA 293.1, ~A$200m post-tax) at 15-18x = A$6.2-7.5 gives A$12.2-13.5/security, consistent with the base case. FY0 REVENUE BASE is the proportionally consolidated 952.1, not the CSV's 556.7 statutory line. FY2026 statutory OCF/FCF (88.8/86.1) are an AASB 10 investment-entity presentation artefact and are not used anywhere in the projection. FY2024 statutory loss (-222.1) was fair-value writedowns over Operating Earnings of 358.7 and is likewise not a trend input. Price 18.26 is the 2026-09-22 ASX close; the stock fell ~8% on 21-Aug-2026 results day because FY27 OEPS guidance (114.0c) excludes performance fees.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (2.9%) diverges >30% from the Operating Earnings 5yr CAGR (11.4%) and both statutory revenue CAGRs are negative: none of the three headline series is a clean growth read. Statutory revenue fell FY22->FY26 because consolidated funds were deconsolidated and development revenue moved off the statutory line (the proportional segment revenue grew 834.2 -> 952.1, +14.1%, in FY26 alone). Statutory EPS swings with fair-value marks (FY24 -0.459). Book equity shrank on the FY24 writedowns and the FY25 A$400m capital reallocation. The selected 6.0% is the distribution-per-security CAGR, the only series management controls and guides (FY27: +6%), and it is used as the long-run anchor the 10-year growth path fades toward; FY27 itself uses the 114.0c OEPS guidance (+10.5%).
historical_growth.notes: fcf_*_cagr are computed on Operating Earnings (FY21 284.3 -> FY23 441.2 -> FY26 488.1), the distributable owner flow, because reported FCF is broken twice: consolidated-fund cash flows before FY23 and the AASB 10 election in FY26. Operating Earnings is post-SBC and post-interest, so no further owner adjustment applies. The FY23 base was a performance-fee peak (OEPS 93.3c after 115.6c in FY22), which is why the 3yr figures are low.

base.growth_rationale: FY27 = OEPS guidance 114.0c (+10.5%, excludes performance fees) reproduced by 10% revenue growth at a 61.0% post-interest margin (OE ~A$538m vs 539m guided). Then fades from FUM-inflow-driven growth toward the 6% distribution CAGR by FY30 and to 3% terminal by FY35, i.e. the platform keeps compounding FUM at a mid-single-digit rate through a normal cycle, with no performance-fee spike.
base.margin_rationale: Post-net-interest EBITDA margin on proportional revenue: FY26 actual 60.8%, FY25 58.7%. Held ~flat then eased 0.5pp for the higher interest cost of gearing that rose 6.0% -> 14.2% in FY26 (A$712m borrowings x ~5.5% is ~A$12m/yr more than FY26 charged).
base.capex_rationale: Net reinvestment of retained earnings (co-investment stakes of 5-20% in new funds, development equity). FY27: OE ~539 less distributions at 53.7c x 473m = 254 -> ~285 retained = 27% of revenue, matching management's 'approximately half of earnings retained'. Fades with growth to 13% of revenue at terminal, where post-tax OE is ~51% of revenue, so terminal retention is ~25% of OE and the 3% terminal growth needs a ~12% incremental return on retained equity (FY26 group ROE on OE 16.8%).

bull.growth_rationale: Post-repricing recovery extends: record equity inflows (A$6.7bn FY26) continue, CCRF scales past A$4bn, sale-and-leaseback and the A$20.4bn development pipeline convert, performance fees return on top of guidance (FY27 beats 114c), and rates ease so co-investment yields and transaction fees both rise. FUM compounds high-single-digit for five years.
bull.capex_rationale: Same retained-earnings deployment in absolute terms early on, but third-party capital does more of the work (fee growth needs only a 5-20% co-investment), so reinvestment as a share of revenue fades faster; terminal retention ~23% of post-tax OE at a ~15% incremental ROE supports 3.5% growth.

bear.growth_rationale: FY27 lands below guidance (7%), then a renewed rate/valuation shock in FY28-29 repeats the FY2023-24 pattern: FUM marked down, inflows stall, transaction and performance fees vanish, office co-investment income falls; proportional revenue drops ~11% over two years, then recovers at a slower trend because investor allocations to Australian office/commercial property reset lower.
bear.margin_rationale: Funds management is a people business with sticky costs (FY26 costs rose 12%); in the downturn revenue falls faster than costs and look-through interest on the co-investments does not fall with rents, so the post-interest margin compresses ~4pp at the trough (FY24 comparable: OE margin fell as interest rose) and only partly recovers.
bear.capex_rationale: Deployment slows in the downturn (committed co-investment calls still fall due in FY27-28, then new fund seeding pauses), and the distribution is held rather than grown; terminal retention ~24% of post-tax OE at a ~10% incremental ROE supports only 2.5% growth.

scenario_narratives.base: Charter Hall delivers FY27 guidance (post-tax OEPS ~114c, +10.5%; DPS +6%) and then compounds Operating Earnings at a fading mid-single-digit rate as Property FUM (A$76bn) grows with institutional and retail inflows through an ordinary cycle, with no performance-fee spike and no valuation shock. Roughly half of earnings continue to be retained and deployed into co-investments and the A$20.4bn development pipeline, so free cash to securityholders starts at the distribution and rises as reinvestment needs fade. The axes that matter are FUM inflows (fee base), the property-yield-to-debt-cost spread (co-investment income and valuations), and whether retained capital keeps earning a mid-teens return.
scenario_narratives.bull: The post-repricing recovery broadens: record inflows continue, CCRF and sale-and-leaseback origination (Sonic, Coles, Woolworths, ALDI) keep adding FUM, the office book's 95% occupancy and 6.2-year WALE hold, rates ease so both co-investment yields and transaction volumes lift, and performance fees return on top of the guided base. Operating Earnings grow double-digit for three years and FUM compounds high-single-digit for five, with third-party capital doing more of the work so reinvestment intensity falls faster. Value is capped at a 20x terminal multiple on free cash to equity.
scenario_narratives.bear: A renewed rate or valuation shock in FY28-29 repeats FY2023-24: FUM is marked down, inflows stall, transaction and performance fees disappear, office co-investment income falls while the look-through interest on those stakes does not. Proportional revenue drops ~11% over two years against a sticky cost base, the post-interest margin compresses ~4pp, and the distribution is held rather than grown. Recovery is at a lower trend because investor appetite for Australian commercial property resets. No solvency question arises (balance-sheet gearing 14.2%), so the bear is an earnings and multiple case, not a survival case.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% default to 25%: the Analysis JSON rates cyclicality, interest-rate sensitivity and fair-value risk all 'high', a FY2024-style down-cycle has occurred within the last three years, and FY27 guidance explicitly strips performance fees because management cannot forecast them. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once (sustained inflows, easing rates, performance fees returning, office holding up) and the stock already fell 8% on the FY26 result when only one of those (costs) disappointed. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Charter Hall is valued on the flow it actually distributes and retains, Operating Earnings, discounted at the AUD cost of equity with no separate debt deduction (the flow is already after look-through interest). The reinvestment that funds growth is charged explicitly, so the growth path is not free; that is the single largest difference from a naive 'all Operating Earnings is free cash' model, which would value the group roughly 60-70% higher. The market at A$18.26 (16x FY27 guided OEPS) is paying for the cycle to keep strengthening and for performance fees to return; the base case does not assume either. Sum-of-parts memo (NTA A$5.95 + funds management at 15-18x post-tax) brackets A$12.2-13.5 and corroborates the base.
key_risks_to_valuation: Reinvestment assumption: if retained capital earns well above the ~12% incremental return implied at terminal (FY26 group ROE on OE was 16.8%), the base case understates value; if it earns less (office writedowns), it overstates.
Discount rate: value is terminal-heavy (Gordon binds in base at 14.7x FCFE); each 1pp on the cost of equity moves the base value ~15%.

Revenue base is proportionally consolidated and includes look-through co-investment income that moves with fund valuations and gearing; a fund-level refinancing at higher rates hits the post-interest margin directly.
Blended cash tax (15%) depends on the trust/company earnings mix; a shift toward taxed funds-management earnings raises it toward 20% (FY25 level).
Performance fees are excluded from guidance and from the base path; they are pure upside in bull and absent in bear.
Proposed tax reforms to stapled/managed-investment structures (cited in the FY26 AR) could raise the effective rate on the trust leg.
